review: 1:1–4 is Psalm 32:1–2 almost word for word (אַשְׁרֵי נְשׂוּי־פֶּשַׁע … אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם לֹא־יַחְשֹׁב יְהוָה לוֹ עָוֺן), because the Arabic طُوبَى لِمَنْ قَدْ غُفِرَتْ لَهُمْ ذُنُوبُهُم is itself quoting that psalm; the Hebrew restores the psalm's own verbs (נָשָׂא, כָּסָה, חָשַׁב) instead of reproducing the Arabic's 'forgiven' twice.

2:1–2 לֹא נִצְדַּקְתִּי בַתּוֹרָה — the Arabic فَلَسْتُ بِالنَّامُوسِ قَدْ صِرْتُ مُبَرَّرًا is Rom 3:20 / Gal 2:16; the Hebrew keeps נָמוֹס as the Greek loan and the Niphal of צָדַק, so justification stays the forensic verb and not a metaphor of 'being made good'.

3:1–4 הוֹפִיעַ הַצֶּדֶק … הָבֶל — the Arabic قَدْ ظَهَرَ الْبِرُّ … وَكُلُّ سَعْيٍ … بَاطِل is Rom 3:21 with Isa 64:5 (וַנְּהִי כַטָּמֵא … כֻּלָּנוּ); הֶבֶל is the Ecclesiastes word for vanity and is kept, since the stanza's claim is that self-righteous striving is not merely insufficient but vapour.

4:1–2 צִדְקִי … פָּעֳלֶךָ — the Arabic أَنْتَ بِرِّي … أَذْكُرُ عَمَلَك is Jer 23:6 (יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ) with Ps 103:2; the Hebrew keeps the possessive suffix on both, so the exchange is personal: His deed, my righteousness.

5:4 בַּמְּנוּחָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה — the Arabic فِي الرَّاحَةِ الْعُلْيَا is the rest of Heb 4:9 (מְנוּחָה) rather than the Sabbath noun שַׁבָּת, so the last stanza names the eschatological rest the epistle names.
